此工作流程专为 Anima Preview3 修复和本地重画而设计，重点关注现有动漫图像内的受控部分编辑。其主要目的是让创作者遮盖特定区域，描述所需的变化，并仅重新生成该局部区域，同时保持图像的其余部分稳定、连贯和视觉一致。

该工作流程使用anima-preview3-base.safetensors作为主要生成模型，qwen_3_06b_base.safetensors作为文本编码器，qwen_image_vae.safetensors作为VAE。它将图像加载、蒙版输入、蒙版扩展、模糊蒙版混合、潜在编码、差分扩散、提示生成、采样、VAE 解码、预览和最终保存结合到一个实用的本地编辑管道中。与普通的图像到图像工作流程相比，当您不想重绘整个图像时，此设置更合适。您只想修改一个选定区域。

此工作流程的关键部分是修复蒙版路线。源图像加载其掩码，然后通过 image_scale_pixel_v2 将图像和掩码标准化为模型友好的尺寸。然后通过 GrowMaskWithBlur 处理蒙版，它会扩展并柔化所选区域。这很重要，因为硬掩模边缘通常会产生可见的接缝，而稍微扩展和模糊的掩模为模型提供了足够的过渡空间，以便将新内容自然地融入到原始图像中。

然后，工作流程使用 VAEEncode 将源图像转换为潜在空间，并使用 SetLatentNoiseMask 来限制重画区域。这意味着采样器被引导聚焦于屏蔽区域，而不是自由改变整个帧。 DifferentialDiffusion 节点进一步强化了这种局部重画行为，使工作流程更适合精确的动画修复、对象替换、面部调整、发型变化、服装修复、道具替换和小型构图修正。

另一个重要功能是内置的提示生成逻辑。该工作流程包括一个 LLM API 提示工程师节点，使用专门用于动画修复和部分重画的角色指令。它分析参考图像，了解整体构图、艺术风格、灯光、姿势、环境和视觉色调，然后将用户的简短编辑指令转换为单个英文提示行。这很有用，因为本地重画提示需要比正常生成提示更加小心。他们必须描述新区域，同时保留图像的其余部分。

工作流程中的示例指令是“仅修改指定区域：将头部更改为菠萝”。这清楚地显示了预期用途：用户提供一个简短的本地编辑请求，LLM 将其重写为模型友好的修复提示，Anima Preview3 执行遮罩重绘，同时保持原始图像身份、风格、光照和周围细节。

采样阶段使用 ClownsharKSampler_Beta，具有 30 步 beta57 设置，CFG 约为 3，以及完整的局部重绘降噪设置。这为遮罩区域提供了足够的自由度来改变，而未遮罩区域仍然受到遮罩和潜在结构的保护。负面提示抑制了常见的动画生成问题，例如低质量、模糊的输出、糟糕的手、畸形的四肢、重复的元素、变形的面部、文本和水印伪影。

此工作流程非常适合需要干净的 Anima Preview3 本地重绘设置来修复细节、替换对象、编辑角色部分、修改配件、修复小视觉问题、测试有趣的本地转换或准备精美的 Civitai 预览图像的创作者。如果您想了解遮罩、LLM 提示重写、差分扩散、Anima Preview3 模型和最终修复输出如何协同工作，请观看上面 YouTube 链接中的完整教程。

This workflow is designed for Anima Preview3 inpainting and local redraw, focusing on controlled partial editing inside an existing anime image. Its main purpose is to let creators mask a specific region, describe the desired change, and regenerate only that local area while keeping the rest of the image stable, coherent, and visually consistent.

The workflow uses anima-preview3-base.safetensors as the main generation model, qwen_3_06b_base.safetensors as the text encoder, and qwen_image_vae.safetensors as the VAE. It combines image loading, mask input, mask expansion, blurred mask blending, latent encoding, Differential Diffusion, prompt generation, sampling, VAE decoding, preview, and final saving into one practical local-editing pipeline. Compared with a normal image-to-image workflow, this setup is more suitable when you do not want to redraw the whole image. You only want to modify one selected area.

The key part of this workflow is the inpainting mask route. The source image is loaded with its mask, then passed through image_scale_pixel_v2 to normalize the image and mask into a model-friendly size. The mask is then processed by GrowMaskWithBlur, which expands and softens the selected area. This is important because hard mask edges often create visible seams, while a slightly expanded and blurred mask gives the model enough transition space to blend the new content naturally into the original image.

The workflow then uses VAEEncode to convert the source image into latent space and SetLatentNoiseMask to restrict the repainting area. This means the sampler is guided to focus on the masked region instead of freely changing the entire frame. The DifferentialDiffusion node further strengthens this local redraw behavior, making the workflow more suitable for precise anime inpainting, object replacement, facial adjustment, hairstyle changes, clothing fixes, prop replacement, and small composition corrections.

Another important feature is the built-in prompt-generation logic. The workflow includes an LLM API prompt engineer node, using a role instruction specialized for anime inpainting and partial redraw. It analyzes the reference image, understands the overall composition, art style, lighting, pose, environment, and visual tone, then converts the user’s short edit instruction into a single English prompt line. This is useful because local redraw prompts need to be more careful than normal generation prompts. They must describe the new area while preserving the rest of the image.

The example instruction in the workflow is “only modify the specified region: change the head into a pineapple.” This shows the intended usage clearly: the user provides a short local edit request, the LLM rewrites it into a model-friendly inpainting prompt, and Anima Preview3 performs the masked redraw while maintaining the original image identity, style, lighting, and surrounding details.

The sampling stage uses ClownsharKSampler_Beta with a 30-step beta57 setup, CFG around 3, and a full local redraw denoise setting. This gives the masked region enough freedom to change while the unmasked area remains protected by the mask and latent structure. The negative prompt suppresses common anime-generation issues such as low quality, blurry output, bad hands, malformed limbs, duplicated elements, deformed faces, text, and watermark artifacts.

This workflow is ideal for creators who need a clean Anima Preview3 local redraw setup for fixing details, replacing objects, editing character parts, modifying accessories, repairing small visual problems, testing funny local transformations, or preparing polished Civitai preview images. If you want to see how the mask, LLM prompt rewrite, Differential Diffusion, Anima Preview3 model, and final inpainting output work together, watch the full tutorial from the YouTube link above.
